title: Hulk Smash, Horse Crash: Ramon Routs Sonny While Alan's New Toys Score Right Away
dek: No Banner only HULK hung a week-high 134.4 on The Horse is Hea in the battle of 4-1 teams, while Team Pillbert won its fifth straight with the two players Sonny sent over a week ago.
body: The biggest game of the young season turned out to be a one-sided affair. Ramon's No Banner only HULK beat Sonny's The Horse is Hea 134.4 to 102.58, the top score of the week, and did it with the two best performances in the league: Kenneth Walker III posted 26.9 on a 21.85 projection and Christian McCaffrey added 26.2 on a 19.15 projection. Sonny entered as a 33% underdog and got a strong 22.8 from James Cook III, but Bryce Young scored 19.84 on his bench and the 31.82-point margin left no room for second-guessing to matter anyway. The HULK is 5-1 with 829.4 points, nearly 98 more than anyone else, and its playoff odds are a flat 100%.

The subplot Sonny will not enjoy reading: the trade. George Pickens scored 10.3 on The Horse is Hea's bench and Ollie Gordon II put up a zero, while Chuba Hubbard (18.6) and DeVonta Smith (17) combined for 35.6 points in Alan's starting lineup. That's how Team Pillbert beat Randy's The fumblers 107.06 to 85.5 as a 59% favorite, with Javonte Williams chipping in 12 against the team that traded him. Alan has won five straight, sits at 5-1, and his title odds now read 26%, up from 16% a week ago. The oddity of the week is that the HULK won by 31 and still saw its title odds slip from 55% to 50%, which is what happens when the second-best team keeps getting better.

Randy's slide has reached three games. Derrick Henry managed 4.5 points on a 17.6 projection, and Trevor Lawrence scored 27.34 on The fumblers' bench, a number larger than the 21.56-point margin of defeat. Stefon Diggs added 13.4 from the bench as well, so the lineup decisions did no favors. The fumblers are still fourth at 3-3, but their playoff odds have dropped to 34%, behind two teams with 2-4 records, and their title odds are down to 2%. Randy's moves this week were a Rams D/ST for Raiders D/ST swap and cutting kicker Brandon Aubrey.

Mekhi's Dawgs beat Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN 105.6 to 83.44 as a 64% favorite, and the waiver wire got the assist: Malik Nabers, added last week, delivered 22.5 on a 14.6 projection. Kyren Williams sputtered to 8.2 on a 19.17 projection, and in a twist that only a fantasy football god with a sense of humor could arrange, Tyler Shough scored 26.96 on the bench one week after posting -0.16 as Kai's starter. Mekhi won anyway, and Dawgs are 2-4 with 36% playoff odds. For Zoe, Bijan Robinson's 6.3 on a 21.34 projection was the week's biggest bust, and the rookie is 2-4 with 5% playoff odds after two straight losses.

Zoe did make the week's boldest quarterback call, dropping Lamar Jackson and adding Jordan Love for Blake Corum. A Wisconsin native picking up the Packers quarterback in a league full of Chicagoans is either a strategic decision or a declaration of war, and Z² is not saying which. Either way, she needs Love to deliver fast, because Team Pillbert is next.

Kaushal's Habibsters beat Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 100.5 to 92.72 as a 70% favorite, and the waiver desk earned its keep. Drake Maye, added this week in place of Sam Darnold, scored 23.8 on a 20.25 projection, the third-best line in the league. Habib was busy beyond that: Woody Marks came in for Keenan Allen and then went out for Tony Pollard, Rico Dowdle and Rome Odunze were cut, and Juwan Johnson arrived shortly after Sonny let him go. Jordan got a big day from Bhayshul Tuten (22.7 on an 11.69 projection) and 20.9 from Isaiah Likely, but Emeka Egbuka scored 14.3 on the bench while Denzel Boston started and posted 2, a 12.3-point gap in a game decided by 7.78. JMoney's team is 1-5 with 0% playoff odds, and Habibsters are 2-4 with 41% playoff odds, the best of any team below .500.

The rest of the transaction log tells you who is shopping. Sonny dropped Jalen Hurts, added Jameson Williams, swapped Juwan Johnson for Pat Freiermuth, and replaced the Bears D/ST with the 49ers D/ST, a move a few Chicago purists might attribute to too many years around Boston. Alan added Josh Jacobs, Tank Dell, Brenton Strange and Dameon Pierce while cutting Tyreek Hill and Odell Beckham Jr., which is a lot of rebuilding for a team that hasn't lost since Week 1. The title picture is now a two-team story with a third act: HULK 50%, Team Pillbert 26%, The Horse is Hea 11%, and nobody else above 6%.

Week 7 serves up The fumblers against The Horse is Hea, where Randy tries to stop a three-game skid and Sonny tries to stop a one-game skid from becoming a trend. Dawgs and Habibsters, both 2-4 and both coming off wins, meet in a game that might as well be a playoff play-in for the fourth seed. Zoe and her new quarterback take on Team Pillbert's five-game streak, and the HULK hosts Jordan, who will need Tuten and Likely to do it all again against the league's top scoring offense.

trade_watch.take: Week one went exactly as the skeptics feared: Hubbard and Smith dropped 35.6 in Alan's lineup during a win, while Pickens sat on Sonny's bench with 10.3 and Gordon scored zero in a 31.82-point loss. A lopsided-looking deal just got more lopsided.

Hubbard has now scored 44 points since this swap, none of them for Sonny, and he spent this week helping Alan instead. Rashee Rice is still on zero for the HULK, so the only winner here is a third team that wasn't part of the deal.

The head-to-head rematch went to Alan: Javonte Williams started and added 12 against his old team, pushing him to 54 since the trade. Diggs scored 13.4 for Randy but did it on the bench, and still has just 6 lineup points to his name.
Mekhi keeps pulling ahead on this one: Adams (5.4) and Jeanty (13.8) both started and are up to 48 combined for Dawgs, while Jefferson put up a zero and remains stuck on 15.8 for Alan.
Still Jordan's deal, with Likely's 20.9 pushing him to 47.8, but this week showed a downside: Egbuka scored 14.3 on the bench while Boston started for 2 in a 7.78-point loss.

bios.1: Sonny's 4-1 start hit a wall against the HULK, a 31.82-point loss with Pickens and Bryce Young scoring on the bench. At 4-2 the playoff odds are a healthy 86%, but title odds slid from 18% to 11%. Jalen Hurts is gone, Jameson Williams is in, and Randy is up next.
bios.2: Randy has lost three straight and fell to 3-3 after Derrick Henry managed 4.5 and Trevor Lawrence's 27.34 sat on the bench. He still holds fourth place, but playoff odds of 34% trail two 2-4 teams. A visit from The Horse is Hea is next.
bios.3: Jordan got 22.7 from Bhayshul Tuten and 20.9 from Isaiah Likely but still fell 100.5 to 92.72, with Egbuka's 14.3 stuck on the bench. At 1-5 the playoff odds have hit 0%. Next up is the HULK, so the goal is a spoiler run.
bios.4: Alan has won five straight and sits at 5-1, and his newest trade paid off immediately with Hubbard and Smith combining for 35.6. Title odds jumped from 16% to 26%, second only to the HULK. He's still reshaping the roster too, adding Josh Jacobs and cutting Tyreek Hill.
bios.5: Mekhi bounced back with a 105.6-point win over Ghostu-Spider SZN, led by waiver add Malik Nabers' 22.5. The quarterback timing remains cursed, with Tyler Shough scoring 26.96 on the bench, but Dawgs are 2-4 with 36% playoff odds. Habibsters come next in a battle of 2-4 teams.
bios.6: Kaushal's waiver churn finally produced a hit, with new quarterback Drake Maye posting 23.8 in a win over Jordan. At 2-4 with 677.9 points, Habibsters have the best playoff odds of anyone under .500 at 41%. Next week's meeting with Dawgs is essentially a play-in game.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut is 5-1 with 829.4 points, nearly 98 clear of the field, after flattening The Horse is Hea with a week-high 134.4. Walker and McCaffrey went one-two in the league, and playoff odds are locked at 100%. The only thing slowing the HULK down is Team Pillbert creeping into its share of the title pie.
bios.8: Zoe has dropped two straight and sits 2-4 after Bijan Robinson's 6.3-point dud. Playoff odds are down to 5%, and she made a big swing by cutting Lamar Jackson for Jordan Love. Team Pillbert's five-game streak is the next hurdle.
